inputs.text: Harry Wait was rightly found guilty of seeking ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent. That is a serious breach of the rules and of voters’ trust. But officials shouldn’t use one man’s misconduct as a shield against legitimate questions about election security. A trustworthy system can withstand lawful scrutiny—and those in authority have a duty to address any real weaknesses, not dismiss concerns to protect their own standing.

output.main_topic: Election security scrutiny following Harry Wait’s ballot-seeking misconduct
